label: STOPP E4
title: NSAID with reduced kidney function
statement: NSAID’s if eGFR < 50 ml/min/1.73m² (risk of deterioration in renal function).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: An anti-inflammatory pain medicine (NSAID) can make kidney function worse, so it should be avoided when the eGFR is already below 50.

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.meets: below 50 mL/min/1.73 m² on the latest result that applies to the course being assessed

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only if the patient is aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown, ask for age confirmation before assessing the supply. For a systemic NSAID (Group A), use the latest eGFR that applied during the course, including a result before supply if it still applies. A result measured after the course ended cannot establish a finding for that course. Below 50 mL/min/1.73 m², report a finding and cite the supply and result. At 50 or above, there is no finding for that course. If the value is unknown or its timing is unclear, report only a possible finding and name eGFR as the missing fact. Ask for the result that applied during treatment. Use the test date or a confirmed link to treatment, never the date the pharmacist entered the answer.
cannot_be_seen: The latest kidney test if none is on the record, how often the NSAID is really taken, anti-inflammatory medicines bought without a prescription, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the NSAID is still needed at the current eGFR, and a review of kidney function.
